facts.text: Forest Hills was founded in 1956 on Nashville’s south side, emerging from suburban residents’ push for local control.
The city’s name reflects its rolling terrain, with the south‑central area once fertile farmland in the Otter Creek watershed.
The McCrory‑Mayfield House at 1280 Old Hickory Boulevard, built in 1798, is the oldest building in Forest Hills and sits on the National Register of Historic Places.
In 2005, the John C. Lovell Bikeway opened, honoring the former Vice Mayor who helped make the trail a reality after a decade of planning.
Forest Hills operates its own municipal government under a general‑law manager–commission charter, keeping independent governance separate from Nashville’s metropolitan system.
